questions.q: How does a set differ from a group?
options: A set flags each member as in/out of a condition without renaming anything; a group relabels combined members into one new name
A set and a group are exactly the same feature with two names
A set can only be used on measures, while a group can only be used on dimensions
A group is always dynamic, while a set is always fixed
questions.explain: A group combines members under one new name (Bookcases and Tables become "Bookcases & Tables"); a set tags each member True/False for membership without renaming anything.

questions.q: What happens to a fixed set when new data is added to the underlying source?
options: Nothing automatically — the fixed set keeps exactly the manually checked members until you edit it yourself
It automatically re-checks every new member against the original condition
It deletes itself and must be recreated
It converts itself into a dynamic set
questions.explain: A fixed set is a frozen, manually checked list — new data never joins it automatically. Only a dynamic set re-evaluates as data changes.

questions.q: Which tab in the Create Set dialog builds a dynamic set?
options: The Condition tab (or the Top tab), defining a rule Tableau re-evaluates against live data
The General tab, where you manually check members
There is no tab for dynamic sets — all sets are fixed
The Format tab
questions.explain: The Condition tab (e.g. "Sum of Sales >= 100,000") and the Top tab (e.g. "Top 10 by Sales") both produce dynamic sets, recalculated as the data changes; the General tab produces a fixed set.

questions.q: What is an important limitation of dynamic sets?
options: A dynamic set can only be based on a single dimension
A dynamic set can never be dragged onto Color
A dynamic set cannot be used in a calculated field
A dynamic set only works with date fields
questions.explain: Dynamic sets are limited to a single dimension. A rule spanning multiple dimensions usually calls for a calculated field or an LOD expression instead.

questions.q: Where does a newly created set appear in Tableau Desktop?
options: Under its own "Sets" heading in the Data pane, with a distinctive set icon
It doesn't appear anywhere until you build a worksheet with it
Only inside the Analytics pane
Sets replace the original field in the Data pane and the original disappears
questions.explain: Every set you create shows up under a dedicated "Sets" section in the Data pane, separate from the original field it was built on.
